newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PLDT global bond seen launching in Feb.
newsitem.headline: PLDT global bond seen launching in Feb.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) has mandated Citicorp International and Goldman Sachs to arrange a bond issue for launch in February, bankers said Wednesday.
Roadshows are scheduled to begin in the second week of February and launch is expected at the end of that month.
The structure of the bond has not been finalised, but traders have speculated that the bond may be about US$300 million in size and carry a maturity of seven to 10 years.
PLDT said last November that it planned to float US$250 million to US$350 million worth of global bonds by the first quarter of 1997.
Bankers said one possible structure for the bond would allow the issuer to reduce the coupon in the event its credit ratings are upgraded by the major agencies.
The structure would be transparent, meaning investors would know at the launch of the issue the yield to maturity if they held onto the bond for its entire life.

"The issuer is taking the position that it does not mind paying a premium today if it believes that in three years or so its ratings will be higher and it will get a benefit in terms of lower interest costs," a banker explained.
PLDT currently is rated equally with the sovereign at Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB by Standard and Poor's Corp.
The bond will be fully registered in the U.S.
